column3: Now receive the one who is weak in faith, but not for disputes over opinions.
One person believes they may eat all things, but the one who is weak eats vegetables.
Let the one who eats not despise the one who does not eat, and let the one who does not eat not judge the one who eats, for God received that person.
Who are you who judges another’s household servant? To that servant’s own master they stand or fall. And they will stand, for the Lord is able to make them stand.
One person judges one day above another, while another judges every day alike. Let each be fully convinced in their own mind.

The one who regards the day regards it for the Lord. And the one who eats eats for the Lord, for that person gives thanks to God; and the one who does not eat does not eat for the Lord and gives thanks to God.
For none of us lives to oneself, and none dies to oneself.
For if we live, we live to the Lord, and if we die, we die to the Lord. Therefore whether we live or die, we belong to the Lord.
For to this end Christ died and lived, so that he might be Lord of both the dead and the living.
But you, why do you judge your brother or sister? Or you also, why do you despise your brother or sister? For we will all stand before the judgment seat of God.
For it is written, “As I live, says the Lord, every knee will bow to me, and every tongue will confess to God.”
So then each of us will give an account concerning oneself.
Therefore let us no longer judge one another, but judge this instead: not to place a stumbling block or trap before a brother or sister.
I know and am convinced in the Lord Jesus that nothing is unclean in itself; but to the one who considers something unclean, to that person it is unclean.
For if your brother or sister is grieved because of food, you are no longer walking according to love. Do not destroy by your food the one for whom Christ died.
Therefore do not let your good be spoken of as evil.
For the kingdom of God is not eating and drinking, but righteousness and peace and joy in the Holy Spirit.
For the one serving Christ in this is pleasing to God and approved by people.
So then let us pursue the things of peace and the things for building up one another.
Do not tear down the work of God for the sake of food. All things indeed are clean, but it is evil for the person who eats through a stumbling block.
It is good not to eat meat nor drink wine nor do anything by which your brother or sister stumbles.
The faith that you have, keep to yourself before God. Blessed is the one who does not judge oneself in what one approves.
But the one who doubts is condemned if they eat, because it is not from faith; and everything not from faith is sin.
